+# Acceptance Criteria
+
+Rules:
+
+- Criteria lines use the exact format `- ACn: <criterion>`.
+- Every criterion ends with [verify: exec `<command>`],
+  [verify: invariant `<command>`], [verify: judged] or
+  [verify: none — <reason>].
+- After `flow freeze` this file is checksum-protected: any edit outside
+  `keryx flow ac update` fails every gate and status transition.
+- Completion requires every ACn to be confirmed via
+  `keryx flow ac confirm <id> <ACn>`.
+
+## Criteria
+
+- AC1: When the pull request is open with the reviewed base and a different head, the `desk-publish` preview returns `headMoved` with both commits, verdict `comment`, inline off, and a body whose first line names the reviewed commit and says the pull request moved on; submit posts a `COMMENT` review with `commit_id` equal to the reviewed head. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/desk-publication.test.ts`]
+- AC2: With a moved head, a submit whose settings ask for another verdict or inline comments still posts a `COMMENT` with no inline comments; a head that moved again after the preview fails with `stale:` and posts nothing; automatic publication with a moved head posts nothing; a changed base or a closed pull request keeps today's refusal. · sensitive: failure-scenario [verify: exec `bun test src/review/desk-publication.test.ts`]
+- AC3: The publish dialog with a moved head shows both commits, disables the verdict choice and inline comments, and labels the primary action "Publish as is for" the short reviewed commit; with the current head the dialog is unchanged. [verify: exec `sh -c 'cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review/ReviewRuns.dom.test.tsx'`]
+- AC4: `on_head_move` has the values `ask`, `follow`, `ignore`; a manual review defaults to `ask` and a rule-triggered review to `follow`; a missing or unknown stored value reads as the default. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/head-move.test.ts`]
+- AC5: The previous-attempt selection accepts the newest partial attempt with accepted findings and an attempt run with different settings, and rejects imported, failed, cancelled and unreviewed attempts. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/update-round.test.ts`]
+- AC6: `findPreviousRound` still chooses a previous round recorded under different review settings. [verify: exec `bun test src/review/prior-round.test.ts`]
+- AC7: "Review again" on a card with an outdated review starts an update round of the same Review on the current head, with the previous round's findings attached. [verify: none — blocked on stage 2 rounds; criterion is rewritten with its test when item 3 is implemented]
+- AC8: Backend review tests, the Desktop review suite, typecheck and lint pass on the branch; the attention-set code, `attachBadges`/`localBadge` and the toolbar container queries are unchanged by this flow. [verify: invariant `sh -c 'bun test src/review && cd apps/desktop && bun test src/review && cd ../.. && bun run typecheck && bunx eslint src/review apps/desktop/src/review && git diff --quiet origin/main -- apps/desktop/src/review/ReviewBoard.tsx src/review/board-badges.ts apps/desktop/src/styles/review.css'`]
+- AC9: The scenario on a real pull request with a commit pushed during a round, then published as is from Desktop. [verify: judged]

+4. [1.609] Theme switch repaints already-rendered chrome via old-slot value matching (lesson/accepted) - lessons/theme-switch-repaint.md
+   `/theme` in the OpenTUI shell applied and persisted correctly on 0.2.66, but `applyTheme` (src/tui/shell-chrome.ts) only recolored the chrome's OWN surfaces (renderer background, sidebar border, docks, composer, `/`-menu). Every renderable painted EARLIER with `getTheme()` — transcript frames (user echoes, code-segment boxes, block bodies, side-worker boxes), tone-colored block headers (`theme.error`/`theme.tool`), dock/queue-dock buttons, sidebar panels — kept the old palette's hex in its `borderColor`/`backgroundColor`/`fg` props, so a dark→dark switch (groknight↔tokyonight) looked like "the theme did not apply". Fix: on every `applyTheme`, walk the renderable trees (transcript, docks, sidebarTop, menu, composer, header, footer) and rewrite any prop whose color equals an OLD theme slot hex to the NEW slot hex.

+# Desktop Review v2 stage 3: head move
+
+## Problem
+
+When the head of a pull request moves after a Desktop review finished, the review can no longer be published at all: `desk-publish` reports "The pull request is closed or its revision moved" and only a local save remains (spec O8). There is no `on_head_move` setting, and "Review again" starts an unrelated run instead of an update round of the same review. The previous-round rules reject a partial round and a round run with different settings (spec O10).
+
+Source: `docs/requirements/keryx-desktop-review-v2/` (PRD R9, R10; specification "Поведение при смене head"; implementation plan v0.1.3, stage 3, owner decisions D1 and D2).
+
+## Expected outcome
+
+1. The publish dialog offers the D1 variants when the head moved after the reviewed commit: "Publish as is for `<sha>`" is allowed only with the verdict Comment and a first body line that names the reviewed commit and says the pull request moved on. Save locally and Skip stay as they are. Automatic publication still refuses a moved head.
+2. `on_head_move` exists as a typed setting with the values `ask`, `follow`, `ignore`; a manual review defaults to `ask` (D2), a rule-triggered review to `follow`.
+3. "Review again" becomes an update round of the same Review (blocked on stage 2, see below).
+4. The previous-round choice accepts a partially completed round and a round run with other settings, with tests.
+
+## Dependency on stage 2
+
+Stage 3 requires stage 2 (flow 519, branch `feat/desktop-review-v2-stage2`): the update round belongs to the Review entity and its rounds, which stage 2 introduces. The operator chose to start stage 3 before stage 2 lands. Items 1, 2 and the round-independent part of 4 are built first, shaped so they attach to rounds without a rewrite. Item 3 and the parts of item 4 that need rounds (wiring the selection into the run start, the package trust rule) wait for stage 2's rounds migration; this flow records them as blocked until then. No rounds schema is invented here.
+
+## Out of scope
+
+- The Reviews tab, the `reviews` table and the migration (stage 2).
+- Wave-boundary head checks in the executor and the `review-orchestrator` "Head moved" procedure (stage 4 for the skill; executor checks go with item 3).
+- Carrying finding answers across the update round (goes with item 3).

+## Approach
+
+### A. Publish as is for the reviewed commit (D1) — `src/review/desk-publication.ts`, `desk-publication-types.ts`, `apps/desktop/src/review/ReviewPublishDialog.tsx`
+
+- The server classifies the PR against the run: `current` (open, same base and head), `head-moved` (open, same base, different head), or `moved` (closed, or the base changed). Only `head-moved` gets the new variant; `moved` keeps today's refusal.
+- `PublicationState` gains `headMoved?: { reviewedHead: string; currentHead: string }`. Its presence means "this draft is the as-is variant for the reviewed commit".
+- In the `head-moved` case the server forces the verdict to `comment` and inline comments off (the current PR diff does not place lines on the old commit), and prepends one first line to the body: ``Reviewed commit `<reviewedHead>`. The pull request has moved to `<currentHead>` since; this review does not cover the newer commits.`` The current head is part of the digest, so a further push makes the preview stale.
+- Submit re-verifies the subject: open, base unchanged, head equal to the previewed current head (a new helper next to `verifyDeskSubject`, which stays strict for every other caller). `commit_id` stays the reviewed head.
+- `automatic` publication with a moved head stays refused.
+- The dialog shows a status line naming both commits, disables the verdict choice and the Inline checkbox, and labels the primary button "Publish as is for `<short sha>`". An optional `onUpdateReview` prop renders "Update review to `<short sha>`" as the first action when a caller provides it; no caller provides it until item 3.
+
+### B. `on_head_move` (D2) — new `src/review/head-move.ts`
+
+- `ON_HEAD_MOVE = ["ask", "follow", "ignore"]`, `type OnHeadMove`, `defaultOnHeadMove(source)` (`manual` and `existing` → `ask`, `scheduled` → `follow`), `parseOnHeadMove(value, source)` (unknown or missing → default; this is how stage 2 reads a nullable column), and `headMoveResponse(mode, phase)` encoding the spec table (running: ask → offer "update after" and "stop and restart"; follow → queue update after finish; ignore → nothing).
+- No storage. Stage 2 adds the `reviews.on_head_move` column and reads it through `parseOnHeadMove`.
+
+### C. Previous-round selection (item 4, round-independent part) — new `src/review/update-round.ts`
+
+- `selectPriorAttempt(attempts)` over `DeskRun` records (an Attempt keeps the `DeskRun` format per the spec): newest attempt, not `existing`, of the current scope, with a recorded reviewed range and accepted findings, state `completed` or `partial`; the options key is ignored. Returns the attempt and `partial: boolean` (for spec step 4, uncovered area).
+- Not wired into `desk-run-service.ts` yet: today the executor copies only a closed previous package and the package trust rule in `prior-round.ts` requires completion evidence, so wiring it alone would change nothing observable and would half-implement item 3. Wiring plus the trust-rule change go with item 3.
+- `prior-round.test.ts` gains a test that a previous round recorded with different review settings is still chosen (settings are not part of the package candidate), pinning that invariant for the update round.
+
+### D. Item 3 — blocked on stage 2
+
+After A–C, `git fetch origin` and check `feat/desktop-review-v2-stage2` for the rounds migration (`src/review/desk-run-store.ts`). If present, rebase onto it and implement the update round; if not, leave T-item3 blocked and report.
+
+## Trade-offs
+
+- Forcing inline off for the as-is variant loses inline placement; placing lines on an old commit would need its diff and is not needed for a Comment.
+- `headMoved` as a state field instead of a new request kind keeps the request contract and the draft file unchanged; the user's explicit act is pressing the distinctly labelled button, and the digest binds the preview they saw.
+
+## Do not break
+
+- Attention-set logic in `apps/desktop/src/review/ReviewBoard.tsx`: not touched by this plan.
+- `attachBadges` ↔ `localBadge` parity: not touched.
+- Toolbar container queries in `apps/desktop/src/styles/review.css`: not touched.

+| base moved or PR closed | blocked reason as today | — | disabled | as today |
